about: The coverage each assembly must stay at or above. Checked by .github/scripts/coverage-floor.js, which the coverage workflow runs. One entry per assembly, never one number for the repository: the host project's pages and controllers are covered through API tests, and a combined figure would let engine coverage fall while the total held steady.
howToRaise: A floor is measured, never chosen. Run the coverage command below, read the score off the report, round it DOWN to two decimals and write that. Raise a floor in the same change that raises the coverage; a floor above the measured score reds the check immediately, which is the mistake this sentence exists to prevent.
command: dotnet test --configuration Release --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage" --results-directory TestResults && node .github/scripts/coverage-floor.js TestResults

Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.measured: line-rate 0.8894 and branch-rate 0.9545 on the <package> tag of coverage.cobertura.xml, from the command above with --framework net10.0 added, run on Windows. Only that target framework was measured: the machine this was run on has no .NET 9 runtime, so the net9.0 leg of the same command reports that the framework is missing rather than a score. Nothing here claims the two legs agree.
Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.lineNote: Both figures moved DOWN when #68 split the solution, and neither was the suite weakening: the validator, the document, the validation result and the error type are the same code with the same tests, measured under Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.Engine below rather than here. Both moved UP again with #70, and again with the change coalescer in #35, and both of those ARE new tests rather than an accounting change. Two classes hold everything unexecuted in this assembly. Plugin.cs is at line-rate 0.0714 and needs a server to construct. LibraryManagerChangeSource is at line-rate 0: it is a constructor and six event accessors forwarding to the server's own library manager, and the only way to execute one is to hold a real ILibraryManager, which means a running server. What the suite covers instead is the type on the other side of that port, LibraryChangeSubscription, at line-rate 1 and branch-rate 1. PluginServiceRegistrator is at line-rate 1, RuleDocumentStore is at line-rate 1, and LibraryChangeCoalescer is at line-rate 1 and branch-rate 1.
Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.branchNote: Every partially covered branch point left in this assembly is in RuleDocumentStore, at branch-rate 0.875. Plugin.cs, PluginServiceRegistrator, LibraryChangeSubscription, LibraryChangeCoalescer and LibraryManagerChangeSource all report branch-rate 1 over the branches they declare. The report puts what is unexecuted on one line, RuleDocumentStore.cs:128 at condition-coverage 83.33% (10/12), which is the six-clause name check that refuses a name composing into a path outside the store's directory. It short-circuits on the first clause that matches, so a name refused by an early clause never reaches the later ones and no set of inputs lights every slot. The coalescer's three defensive arms are inside that branch-rate 1 rather than outside it, and reaching them is why the suite's fake clock can move without running a timer and can run a timer that is not due: a timer is a request and not a promise, so a callback that arrives early, arrives late or arrives with nothing to do is an ordinary input rather than an impossible one.

The compiler requires it for exhaustiveness and no input reaches it, because a member that is absent is refused before anything describes its kind. Its line number moves whenever anything is added above it in that file and the arm itself has not changed since it was written.
Jellyfin.Plugin.SmartCollections.Engine.lineNote: Both figures moved DOWN when the missed-where loop in MembershipDiff.Between became a Where and a ToList, and that is a denominator rather than a weakening: six executed lines and four covered branch slots left the assembly, so the same single unexecuted line and the same single partial branch point now weigh more. Nothing became unreached and no test was removed. Lines went from 388 of 390 to 382 of 384 and branch slots from 47 of 48 to 43 of 44, counted off the condition-coverage attributes in the same report the rates are read from. Before that the floor was raised in the same change that raised the coverage rather than left where it was, which is what the note above this one asks for. The one line at hits=0 in the whole assembly is RuleDocumentValidator.cs:206, the arm the branch note describes. Everything else is executed, including CollectionRefreshGate, MembershipApplier, ICollectionMembershipWriter, CollectionRefresh, CollectionRefreshOutcome, MembershipDiff, RuleDocument, RuleDocumentValidation and RuleValidationError. One thing worth knowing about the number rather than the code: when #38 put the gate in front of the applier, a run cancelled before it starts stopped entering the applier at all, which left the applier's own rethrow arm unexecuted and the line figure BELOW the floor of the day. What repaired it was not the gate's own lines but the test added with them, which cancels a run while it is writing.
